_about: Police dispatch pre-alerts (sizeup/intel/engine.py). Generic phrases only: no real addresses, names, callsigns or slang (those live in the hub's Settings, never in this public file). Every category pushes to the pre-alert topic from day one (user, 2026-11-12: no shadow week); Settings > System > Intel moves any rule, category or the pack down the ladder off / shadow / log / map / push. fire_call (a burning smell or smoke complaint, the FD being notified: either alone is under the threshold; with the dispatch cue or each other it is over) holds at log until it has a place a crew can drive to in the source's towns ("place": true). Scope: Port Chester / Rye / Rye Brook PD only (dispatch, tac, secure); the other MRRS police talkgroups (Harrison, MTA, interop) are neighbor_police.json, these same rules at log. Barricade: the word alone ("hostage", "barricade") is under the threshold; with a dispatch cue, or in the same transmission with a weapon, a standoff, ESU / SWAT / a negotiator (within a few words, either order), or said as a barricaded subject or a hostage situation it is over. Never from another transmission's cue: two talkers' words don't make a barricade. Cleared, negated or not a call ("not a hostage situation", "no longer barricaded", "unfounded", "stand down", a parade or detail barricade): no barricade from that transmission ("not" on both barricade rules; a SWAT / ESU / hostage / barricade drill too). Only "drill only", "it's a drill", "just a drill" are suppressed: a bare "drill" never ends a call. Weapons: a weapon involved or held by a person ("male waving a machete", "pulled out a gun", a BB or airsoft gun) is a push alone; never a question, a negative or unknown, the past, a kitchen, a shop or licence, lawful ownership, toys, or equipment of the police's own. Its "deescalate" phrases ("the gun was secured", "the firearm has been recovered") note the open weapons event the row ties to as de-escalated, no push; naming a weapon again clears the note (and pushes again when that row alone is over the threshold). Assault (sexual assault included: the intel topic may carry details) and an out-of-control person (EDP) are under the threshold alone and over it with a dispatch cue; never an arrest, a charge, the past, a report-only call, an animal, a jump start or sport; an armed one is the weapons call's and one in progress ("he's choking her") a dispute (safety). Officers assaulted or down are their own safety category. Weapons, EDP, dispute, assault and the category for officers tie a later row by their telling words only ("words"): a disregard or a unit's move with common words never reaches them. The dispatch cue knows more dispatcher wording ("can you respond", "units responding", "the complainant states", "be advised"). The local model behind the rules (sizeup/intel/backing.py) raises a category only when the trigger, the dispatch just before it, or two context transmissions say one of its "model_cues" (every category but aided and alarm): the model's answer alone over-flags routine traffic.

label: PD

fire_report.label: Smoke / fire reported
fire_report.describe: Smoke or fire seen or reported: a building, vehicle, brush or dumpster burning, smoke showing from a structure.

fire_call.label: Burning smell / FD notified
fire_call.describe: A smell of smoke or burning, an appliance or wiring smoking, or police asking for the fire department, no fire seen yet.

weapons.label: Weapon / shots
weapons.describe: A weapon shown, used or reported: shots fired or heard, a person shot or stabbed, someone armed with a gun, blade or other weapon.

escalate: (coming at|came at|charging at|charging|going after|lunging at|lunged at)

mva_injury.label: MVA with injuries
mva_injury.describe: A vehicle crash with someone hurt, trapped or unconscious, or EMS needed; a rollover; a pedestrian or cyclist struck.

barricade.label: Barricade
barricade.describe: A person barricaded or holding hostages, a standoff, a negotiator or tactical team requested.

aided.label: Aided / unresponsive
aided.describe: A medical emergency that is not a crash: a person unresponsive, not breathing, collapsed, overdosed or seriously ill or hurt.

hazmat.label: Gas / hazmat
hazmat.describe: A gas leak or odor of gas, carbon monoxide, a chemical spill or release, a suspicious substance.

water_rescue.label: Water rescue
water_rescue.describe: A person in the water or in trouble on it: someone drowning, a boat in distress, someone through the ice.

pursuit.label: Pursuit
pursuit.describe: Police chasing a fleeing vehicle or person, with the direction or roads given.

edp.label: EDP
edp.describe: A person in a mental health crisis: suicidal, threatening self-harm or to jump, or acting irrationally and dangerously.

dispute.label: Dispute / fight
dispute.describe: A fight or physical dispute in progress, an assault, a large disorderly crowd, a dispute turning violent.

alarm.label: Alarm
alarm.describe: A fire, smoke, CO or burglar alarm sounding, or reported by an alarm company.

assault.label: Assault
assault.describe: An assault reported after the fact or without a weapon: someone punched, beaten, attacked or sexually assaulted.

officer.label: Officer: needs help
officer.describe: Police officers assaulted, hurt, shot, stabbed or down, or calling for urgent help.
